About

Dr. Yuanxiong Guo is an Associate Professor in the Department of Information Systems and Cybersecurity at The University of Texas at San Antonio, with a courtesy appointment in the Department of Electrical Engineering. His research spans machine learning, trustworthy AI, and quantum computing and networking, with a particular emphasis on applications in healthcare, energy, and robotics. He received his Ph.D. in electrical and computer engineering from the University of Florida in 2014.

Dr. Guo is a Senior Member of both ACM and IEEE, and currently serves as an Editor for IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology and for IEEE Transactions on Machine Learning in Communications and Networking. His work has been recognized with endowed research awards at UT San Antonio, an AFRL Visiting Faculty Research Program Award, and a Best Paper Award at IEEE GLOBECOM. His research has been supported by the National Science Foundation, the Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health, AFRL, NVIDIA, and industry partners.

Research Interests

  • Machine Learning

    Large language models, AI agents, federated and multimodal learning

  • Trustworthy AI

    Privacy, fairness, explainability, and safety

  • Quantum Systems

    Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms, distributed quantum computing, and quantum networks

  • Applications

    Digital health, renewable energy, and human-robot collaboration

Recent News

  1. 08/2026

    We are grateful to receive support from the NVIDIA Academic Grant Program to advance our research on generative and agentic AI.

    Congratulations to Tongnian Wang on successfully defending her dissertation and joining the Gary W. Rollins College of Business at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga as a tenure-track Assistant Professor!

  4. 02/2026

    We are excited to launch a new Health Research Challenge project with our clinical collaborators at UT Health San Antonio, focusing on wearable sensors and AI for improved chronic disease management.

  5. 10/2025

    We are excited to launch a new UTSA CONNECT project with Southwest Research Institute on AI-enabled combustion diagnostics and prediction for hydrogen engines.
